title: Elements of a communication system
notes: The elements can be named as transducer, modulator and transmitter, medium, and receiver plus output transducer. This is the same chain as source, transmitter, channel and receiver, with the transducers made explicit.
A microphone is an input transducer: sound pressure becomes a voltage. A loudspeaker is an output transducer: the recovered voltage becomes sound again.
The message signal is often low frequency. Multiplying it with a carrier, or varying the carrier's amplitude or frequency, produces the modulated wave that the antenna launches.

The medium decides the loss. A copper pair, a fibre and a radio path have different attenuation and different noise. The link budget is the comparison of transmitted power with the power the receiver needs.
At the receiver a tuner selects the carrier, a demodulator strips it, and an amplifier raises the message to a useful level. Selecting the wrong carrier selects a different message.
Two-way radio uses the same elements in both directions. Each station is sometimes the source and sometimes the destination.

exercises.question: Identify the input transducer, the medium and the output transducer for a telephone call on a copper line.
steps: The microphone in the handset is the input transducer.
The transmitter circuits send the electrical signal into the copper pair.
The copper pair is the medium, the channel.
The earpiece is the output transducer.
Noise can be induced into the copper pair along the way.
